name: Clone Vat Experiments
desc: Primitive cloning vats repurposed from pre-collapse biotechnology. An early step in mastering human cloning technology. Produces a trickle of cloned adults to supplement natural population growth. These clones are slow-witted and cannot perform tasks as well as their natural counterparts, which incurs a stability penalty. A small specialized nanoforge weaves the tissue the vats grow.

name: Cloning Industry
desc: Facilities and infrastructure for cloning human beings from nothing. These people have not lived a life, but had one simulated by an alpha-level AI. They are frailer than the natural-born and fall to disease and injury far sooner, but the simulated memories leave them much less stunted than earlier clones, and they hold down regular jobs like anyone else. This leads to massively increased population growth. Banks of specialized nanoforges weave biological matter in place of alloys, feeding the vats around the clock.

name: Cloning Megafactory
desc: An industrial-scale cloning operation capable of producing near-human clones. The sheer volume of clone output transforms even a modest colony into a population powerhouse, however, the social cost is extreme - violence, crime and disease run rampant among the clone-majority population. Its specialized nanoforges weave biological matter on an industrial scale.

name: Organ Flashcloning
desc: Cloned organs are perfectly fine substitutes for human organs, allowing surgeons to have a near-endless supply of designer organs, ready to transplant. The vats here never grow a whole person: a specialized nanoforge weaves a single heart, liver or pair of lungs, and flash-growth baths bring it to full size in days. Every organ is matched to its recipient before it is grown, so rejection is a thing of the past. Hospitals that once ran waiting lists now run delivery schedules, and a colony that never has to choose who lives is a calmer one.

name: Marine Sim-Cloning
desc: Marine clones are grown to fighting age in months, while a training simulator runs them through years of drills, boarding actions and street fighting before they ever open their eyes. Each batch walks out of the vats knowing how to hold a rifle and follow orders. Records from before the Collapse mention a rain-soaked ocean world whose long-necked cloners grew an entire army this way, for a republic that did not survive the war the army was built for. The engineers here keep one rule from that story: no hidden orders in the simulator, and certainly none numbered sixty-six.
